channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Governo corre para evitar derrota na MP do fim da "taxa das blusinhas"
item.description: The Lula government is racing to approve the measure provisory that ends the so-called 'tax on little blouses' before it expires on September 8, pressuring Senate President Davi Alcolumbre to install the required joint committee for voting. The timeline is tight due to the reduced congressional schedule during the election campaign, with only two concentrated voting windows in August and early September. Senate government leader Teresa Leitão has already spoken with Alcolumbre to warn him of the risk of the MP lapsing.

item.title: Trump prefere guerra ideológica com Brasil a interesse estratégico dos EUA no país, diz analista
item.description: Analyst Anthony Pereira argues that Donald Trump is prioritizing an ideological war against Brazil over U.S. strategic interests in the country, exacerbating tensions with the Lula government. He warns that the influence of figures like Trump and Javier Milei is deepening regional polarization, posing serious risks to Brazilian democracy ahead of the 2026 elections. Pereira cautions that this dynamic could empower authoritarian forces and undermine democratic institutions in Brazil.

item.title: Marcola e Lulinha: campanha de Lula tem semana de crise e mede impacto
item.description: Lula's campaign faces crisis after revelations that advisor Marcola received R$ 249,000 from lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger, who claims it was a private loan. Marcola stepped down to avoid further damage, while PF investigations against Lulinha, the president's son, continue with three STF-authorized inquiries into suspected influence peddling. Allies are divided on electoral impact, with some downplaying the episode and others viewing it as unnecessary damage.

item.title: Haddad quer paternidade da Carbono Oculto e mira despesas de Tarcísio
item.description: Fernando Haddad (PT) will unveil his public security plan this Saturday, claiming 'paternity' of the Carbono Oculto operation and criticizing Tarcísio de Freitas for increasing police lethality without reducing organized crime. The campaign will also challenge what it deems unnecessary state expenditures, including the R$ 3.7 billion advance for Metro Line 6, R$ 2.5 billion paid to highway concessionaires for pandemic-related losses, and the no-bid Muralha Paulista security technology contract.

item.title: Malafaia critica vice de Flávio, mas admite apoio por falta de opção
item.description: Pastor Silas Malafaia criticized the selection of Alfredo Gaspar as Flávio Bolsonaro's running mate for breaking the promise to name a woman and for involving the candidate in a suspected rape of a minor case now under review by the STF. Despite the legal controversies and ally discomfort, Malafaia admitted he will support the ticket due to lack of viable alternatives on the right, as polls show conservative voters are regrouping around Flávio to face Lula in a potential runoff.

item.title: Prefeito ameaça demitir servidores que não votarem em Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The mayor of Campestre do Maranhão, Fernando Bermuda (PSB), threatened to dismiss municipal employees who do not support Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) in the 2026 elections, using WhatsApp messages and a religious gathering to pressure voters. He stated that those who vote for Lula will be 'on the street' and promoted an AI-generated song linking job retention to support for the Bolsonaro candidate. Employees reported the behavior is recurrent, based on threats and ignorance.

item.title: Governo Lula vê influência de Trump em crise com Milei e Argentina
item.description: The Lula government believes the diplomatic crisis with Argentina, sparked by Javier Milei’s criticisms of Brazil, is part of a U.S. strategy to influence Brazil’s 2026 elections. The tension with Buenos Aires, which led to a downgrade in diplomatic relations, coincides with friction with Paraguay and is seen as part of a broader U.S. effort to pressure Brazil through regional allies aligned with Trump.

item.title: Áudios de Luchsinger para ex-empregada mostram convívio com Lulinha
item.description: Audio messages obtained in the labor lawsuit filed by former domestic worker Zildeni Gomes reveal that Fábio Luís Lula da Silva, known as Lulinha, frequently visited the Brasília residence of lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger, including using the children's bedroom for guests. The messages, attached to the case, indicate daily interaction and refer to Lulinha as the 'little friend' of the former employee. The case is connected to STF investigations into alleged influence peddling involving both individuals.

item.title: João Paulo Cunha volta à política 750% mais rico. Jean Wyllys, 80% mais pobre
item.description: Former deputy João Paulo Cunha (PT), convicted in 2012 for passive corruption and money laundering, returns to politics with assets up 750% since then, rising from R$375,000 to R$3.1 million, largely due to a Brasília property. His running mate, Jean Wyllys (PT), saw an 80% drop in declared assets, falling from R$1.2 million to R$250,000. Singer Netinho de Paula (MDB) also re-enters politics with modest assets of R$50,700, far below his performance fee.

item.title: Aliados de Lula querem usar Datena para atacar Flávio na TV
item.description: Allies of President Lula proposed using TV presenter José Luiz Datena as a central figure in the Workers' Party's electoral broadcasts to attack Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, leveraging Datena's credibility from police programs to expose allegations, such as Flávio's alleged ties to banker Daniel Vorcaro of Banco Master. The idea serves as a counter to Flávio's campaign strategy, which plans to deploy his running mate, deputy Alfredo Gaspar, to attack Lula's allies, including Lulinha, Frei Chico, and Marcola. Datena, who left EBC in June to run for federal deputy under the PSB of São Paulo, would be used to lend weight to accusations against Flávio on television.

item.title: Advogado vai ao TSE contra o PL e diz ter sido impedido de concorrer à Presidência
item.description: Lawyer José Adailton Miranda Cavalcante claimed he was blocked from running for president by the PL after the party administratively denied his affiliation, despite his online registration in April 2026. He filed actions with the TSE, including a writ of security, which was rejected by Ministers Kassio Nunes Marques and Dias Toffoli, who argued that electoral justice cannot intervene in internal party matters without direct electoral effects. Cavalcante sought to be included in the pre-candidate list to compete on 'equal footing' with Flávio Bolsonaro, chosen at the PL’s national convention on July 27, 2026.

item.title: Simone Mendes, Titãs e mais: o que fazer no DF neste fim de semana
item.description: The second weekend of August in Brasília features a diverse cultural agenda, highlighted by the Na Praia music festival with Titãs, Os Paralamas do Sucesso, and Nando Reis on Friday, and Simone Mendes and Filho do Piseiro on Saturday. On Sunday, the free Forreggae 2026 Festival takes place at Praça do Cine Itapuã in Gama, headlined by Mato Seco, blending reggae, forró, and DJ sets. Additional events include theater performances, pagode gatherings, and music tours across the Federal District.

item.title: México estrecha los lazos con Brasil en plena escalada de la tensión entre Lula y Trump
item.description: Mexico's Foreign Minister Roberto Velasco visited Brasília to co-chair the VI Meeting of the Mexico-Brazil Binational Commission, amid growing isolation of both countries due to Donald Trump's influence across the Americas. The meeting takes place at a sensitive time for President Lula, who faces heightened tensions with the U.S. following the cancellation of the Brazilian ambassador's visa and is preparing for re-election in 2026.

item.title: De quem é a culpa do gasto de R$ 1,2 trilhão com juros da dívida?
item.description: President Lula advocates for a 'fiscal seriousness' policy to lower interest rates, but criticizes current fiscal rules that limit public spending, arguing they hinder federal government investments. He questions whether the responsibility for the R$1.2 trillion in interest payments on the debt lies with restrictive fiscal rules or the need for greater public investment to stimulate the economy.

item.title: Registro de Jair Renan Bolsonaro no TSE não informa orientação sexual
item.description: Jair Renan Bolsonaro, federal deputy candidate from Santa Catarina, did not disclose his sexual orientation in his TSE candidacy registration, despite declaring himself heterosexual in 2024. The TSE allows candidates to choose whether to disclose sexual orientation, and currently 44.23% of the 8,229 registered candidacies have opted not to disclose it. His registration also confirms he is a cisgender man and single.

item.title: Doce Maravilha 2026: veja os horários de todos os shows do festival
item.description: The Doce Maravilha 2026 festival takes place from August 7 to 9 at the Jockey Club Brasileiro in Gávea, featuring performances by artists such as Caetano Veloso and Emicida, Paulinho da Viola and Maria Bethânia, Djavan and Leci Brandão. Gates open at 5 PM on Friday and 2 PM on Saturday and Sunday, with ticket prices ranging from R$ 218.40 to R$ 515.97. The schedule includes shows across three stages (Bradesco, Corona, and Deezer) with detailed timing for each day.

item.title: Eleições 2026: Com que idade é obrigatório votar?
item.description: In Brazil, voting is mandatory for literate citizens aged 18 to 70. For those aged 16–17, over 70, and illiterate individuals of any age, voting is optional. Failure to vote when required may result in fines or restrictions on obtaining passports, public employment, or participating in public contests.

item.title: Renan Santos, o candidato tigrinho, é a versão 2026 de Pablo Marçal
item.description: Renan Santos, candidate of the Missão party and leader of the MBL troop, is positioning himself as an outsider in the 2026 presidential election, using provocative videos and bold proposals on social media due to lack of TV time. He is compared to Pablo Marçal, the 2022 coach-candidate, as a new iteration of the digital, anti-establishment campaign strategy. The article is subscriber-only and highlights his bet on going viral to gain visibility.

item.title: g1 e GloboNews entrevistam Ronaldo Caiado, candidato à Presidência, nesta sexta; saiba como assistir
item.description: g1 and GloboNews are interviewing presidential pre-candidate Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) this Friday (7) at 2 p.m. in Rio de Janeiro, with live broadcast across their platforms. The interview is part of a series featuring the top five candidates from the July 24 Datafolha poll, following interviews with Renan Santos (Missão) and Romeu Zema (Novo). Lula (PT) declined the invitation, while Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) is scheduled for Monday (10).

item.title: Desenrola para trabalhadores informais deve iniciar com novas regras na semana que vem: veja o que mudou
item.description: The Desenrola program for informal workers, launched over a month ago as part of Lula's re-election strategy, will begin implementation next Monday following rule adjustments requested by Caixa and Banco do Brasil. The changes aim to encourage participation from financial institutions, including private banks that initially rejected the initiative.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro deixa Ciro Nogueira de fora da lista de apoios ao Senado
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro released a list of 47 Senate candidates endorsed by his presidential campaign, excluding PP national leader and Senator Ciro Nogueira, despite earlier efforts to bring the party into his coalition. He announced support state-by-state, endorsing only Tiago Junqueira (PL) in Piauí, where Nogueira is seeking re-election. The exclusion follows Nogueira’s involvement in the Operation Compliance Zero investigation into alleged corruption and money laundering tied to Banco Master, although he denies any wrongdoing.

item.title: Vice de Zema, Eduardo Girão declara R$ 34,1 milhões em bens
item.description: Senator Eduardo Girão (Novo-CE), running mate of Romeu Zema (Novo) in the presidential race, declared R$ 34.1 million in assets to the TSE, including a foreign bank deposit of R$ 9.9 million and business holdings worth R$ 4.2 million. His net worth decreased by R$ 14.1 million since 2024, when he declared R$ 48.2 million in his Fortaleza mayoral campaign. Zema, meanwhile, declared R$ 178 million in assets, 38% more than in 2022.

item.title: PT planeja levar militantes de outros estados a SP para lotar ato de Lula em estádio e evitar fiasco
item.description: The PT plans to mobilize supporters from Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, Paraná, and São Paulo to fill the stadium for Lula's re-election campaign launch, aiming to avoid empty seats that could signal electoral weakness. The strategy seeks to project unity and strength at the outset of the 2026 campaign.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro diz que tentou ter vice mulher e que Alfredo Gaspar foi escolhido em cima da hora
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) stated in his weekly livestream that he attempted to select a woman as his vice-presidential running mate, but the choice ultimately fell to federal deputy Alfredo Gaspar (PL-AL) in a last-minute decision. He explained that the selection was made hastily after facing difficulties in securing a female candidate for the ticket.

item.title: Partido Agir oficializa candidatura de Edjane Lima ao Governo de SP
item.description: The Agir party officially nominated Edjane Lima de Sousa as its candidate for Governor of São Paulo in the 2026 elections, under the ballot name 'Edjane por São Paulo' and the majoritarian slate 'Agir por São Paulo, o melhor para o Brasil'. The running mate for vice-governor remains undecided and will be announced by August 15, the final registration deadline. The party also ratified 67 federal and 33 state deputy candidates, confirmed it will not run presidential or senatorial candidates, but left open the possibility of forming proportional alliances.

item.title: Vitória quebra tabu de quase 10 anos em casa sobre o Athletico-PR
item.description: Vitória ended a nearly 10-year home winless streak against Athletico-PR with a 4-0 victory at Barradão on August 6, 2026, in a Copa do Brasil match. The last time Vitória defeated Athletico-PR in Salvador was in 2016, by a 3-2 score. The win secured Vitória's place in the quarterfinals, awaiting the CBF draw on Tuesday, August 11.

item.title: A queda inédita de Flávio em uma frente estratégica da campanha
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro gained 100,000 new social media followers but recorded his lowest engagement rate in 2026 at just 0.63%, indicating audience growth did not translate into increased interaction. According to Alek Maracajá, CEO of Ativaweb, engagement is a more meaningful metric than follower count for assessing digital political strength, and the decline may be linked to recent campaign events such as the party convention and presidential ticket definition. Lula also shows low engagement (0.45%), highlighting a shared challenge in converting reach into mobilization.

item.title: Em reunião no Alvorada, Lula defende Marcola e concede ‘benefício da dúvida’ a ex-assessor
item.description: In a private meeting at the Palácio da Alvorada, President Lula defended his former chief of staff, Marcola, saying he is giving him the 'benefit of the doubt' regarding transactions under investigation by the Federal Police. The stance comes amid probes into alleged financial irregularities linked to the aide.

item.title: Irmão de candidato ao governo do Amapá é demitido pelo Conselho Nacional do Ministério Público
item.description: The brother of Amapá gubernatorial candidate Dr. Furlan (PSD) was unanimously dismissed by the National Council of the Public Ministry (CNMP) on Thursday, June 6. João Paulo Furlan, a prosecutor in Amapá’s Public Ministry, was removed following a decision by the body overseeing the conduct of Brazilian public prosecutors.

item.title: Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro confirmam presença em debate com seis candidatos
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro confirmed their participation in a televised debate with six candidates for the 2026 elections, organized by RedeTV!. The event marks one of the first direct confrontations between prominent figures from the government and opposition, highlighting the anticipated political polarization ahead of the election.

item.title: Após ‘lavar roupa suja’, Lula e Alcolumbre reabrem diálogo entre Executivo e Senado
item.description: President Lula and Senate President Davi Alcolumbre met in a dinner mediated by STF ministers to ease institutional tensions following a period of friction. The meeting paved the way for a new round of negotiations between the Executive and Legislative branches.

item.title: Zema declara patrimônio de R$ 178 milhões ao TSE
item.description: Romeu Zema, former governor of Minas Gerais and pre-candidate for President from the Novo party, declared to the TSE a net worth of R$ 178 million, an increase of R$ 49 million since 2022. The declaration reflects growth in his assets, though specific details of the composition were not disclosed in the note.

item.title: LIVE POLITICANDO SEGUNDA EDIÇÃO - ELEIÇÕES 2026 - LULA X FLÁVIO BOLSONARO
item.description: The content describes a political live stream titled 'POLITICANDO SEGUNDA EDIÇÃO - ELEIÇÕES 2026 - LULA X FLÁVIO BOLSONARO', accompanied by technical error messages related to YouTube video playback. There is no substantive political discussion, debate, or policy analysis present in the provided text.

item.title: Condenação histórica de Marco Buzzi abre nova fase e pode incentivar mais denúncias
item.description: The Superior Tribunal of Justice has permanently removed Minister Marco Buzzi from office over sexual harassment and importuning charges, a decision deemed historic as it marks the first time a magistrate has been dismissed in Brazil. Minister Luís Felipe Salomão’s vote relied on consistent evidence and testimony, which the defense failed to overturn despite highlighting minor inconsistencies. With the administrative phase concluded, the case moves to the Supreme Federal Court for potential criminal prosecution, using all documentation gathered during the investigation.

item.title: Ao TSE, Zema declara R$ 178 milhões em bens; 38% a mais que em 2022
item.description: Romeu Zema (Novo), presidential candidate, declared R$ 178.7 million in assets to the TSE, a 38% increase from R$ 129 million in 2022. His largest asset is a family holding valued at R$ 94.5 million. In 2022, he was the 15th wealthiest candidate among all offices contested.

item.title: Haddad questiona qualificação do vice de Flávio
item.description: Fernando Haddad (PT), candidate for governor of São Paulo, criticized the choice of Alfredo Gaspar (PL-AL) as vice president on Flávio Bolsonaro’s (PL) presidential ticket, calling it one of the worst choices he could imagine and questioning the audacity of the selection.

item.title: Vice do PT defende Lulinha e diz que filho do presidente vive em ‘condições precárias’ na Espanha
item.description: The vice president of the Workers' Party (PT), Washington Quaquá, stated that President Lula's son, known as Lulinha, lives in 'precarious conditions' in Spain and defended his innocence amid Federal Police investigations. The remarks were made as investigations involving the president and his family continue. The party seeks to mitigate the impact of the allegations.

item.title: Candidata no RS, neta de Brizola critica Caiado: “Concorreu com meu avô”
item.description: During a debate hosted by Rádio Gaúcha, Rio Grande do Sul gubernatorial candidate Juliana Brizola (PDT), granddaughter of former governor Leonel Brizola, criticized presidential candidate Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), stating he 'ran against my grandfather'. The exchange followed a heated argument with Vice Governor Gabriel Souza (MDB), intensifying the debate's tone.

item.title: Flávio recuperou fôlego e Lula não é imbatível, mas muita água (suja) ainda vai rolar
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro has regained momentum in polls, narrowing Lula’s lead, who is no longer seen as unbeatable. Despite controversies surrounding his running mate Alfredo Gaspar (PL-AL) and leaked audios, Flávio has reconciled with Michelle Bolsonaro and mitigated reputational damage. Lula, meanwhile, faces scrutiny over investigations into his son Lulinha and allegations of influence-peddling involving lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger, amid escalating tensions between the PF and STF over the INSS case, heightening political instability.

item.title: Enviado de Putin discute cooperação com Lula
item.description: Nikolai Patrushev, political advisor to Russian dictator Vladimir Putin and former FSB director, visited Brazil for two days this week, stopping in Brasília and Rio de Janeiro. During the trip, he met with President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva to discuss bilateral cooperation between the two countries.

item.title: Veja o que é #FATO e o que é #FAKE na entrevista de Romeu Zema ao g1 e à GloboNews
item.description: The fact-checking team of Fato ou Fake analyzed Romeu Zema's interview on g1 and GloboNews. His claim of governing for seven and a half years without any scandal or corruption was rated #FAKE due to Operation Rejeito, which exposed a billion-dollar corruption scheme in Minas Gerais mining involving his administration's high-ranking officials. His statement about the state's fiscal improvement—from a R$ 11 billion deficit in 2018 to a R$ 5 billion surplus in 2024—was rated #FATO based on official data from SEF-MG.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro diz que indígena não quer ser "animal de zoológico"
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro stated that Indigenous peoples no longer wish to be treated like 'animals in a zoo' and advocates for their inclusion through internet access, citing the Wi-Fi Brasil program as evidence of their demand for connectivity. He pledged to guarantee Indigenous autonomy, allowing communities to control their territories and subsurface resources, including the right to exploit them and receive royalties, under environmental responsibility.

item.title: Justiça e MPs unem forças contra o assédio eleitoral
item.description: The Electoral Justice, Labor Justice, Electoral Public Ministry, and Labor Public Ministry signed a technical cooperation agreement to combat electoral harassment in the workplace, including educational campaigns, training, and sharing of best practices. TSE President Minister Kassio Nunes Marques emphasized that voting is only legitimate when free from economic, hierarchical, or professional pressures, and that such practices undermine democratic integrity.

item.title: Manual do Eleitor: conheça os direitos do eleitorado idoso nas Eleições 2026
item.description: The Voter's Manual for the 2026 Elections outlines specific rights for elderly voters, including priority service at polling stations, with absolute priority for those aged 80 or older. TSE Resolution No. 23.759/2026 and Law No. 14.364/2022 establish these guarantees, extending priority also to companions of elderly voters aged 80 or above. The goal is to ensure a more accessible, safe, and dignified electoral participation for this group.

item.title: Eleições 2026: TSE fecha acordo com ElevenLabs contra deepfakes de voz
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) has signed an agreement with ElevenLabs to combat voice deepfakes in the 2026 elections, creating a list of 'prohibited voices' for candidates and officials. The partnership, which involves no financial transfers, integrates into the Electoral Justice’s Permanent Program to Counter Disinformation and runs until December 31, 2026.

item.title: Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro ficarão lado a lado durante debate Momento da Decisão
item.description: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro will stand side by side in the 'Momento da Decisão' debate on September 14 at 10 p.m., organized by a coalition of media outlets. The debate will feature three segments: candidate-to-candidate questions, journalist questioning, and a final direct confrontation, followed by closing remarks. If a runoff occurs, a second debate is scheduled between October 12 and 19 at the same time.

item.title: Como funciona o Teste de Integridade, “a prova dos nove” da urna eletrônica
item.description: The Integrity Test is a public and mandatory procedure that compares manually recorded paper ballots with the electronic voting machine’s printed result to ensure no vote has been altered. In use since 2002 and regulated by TSE Resolutions No. 23.673/2021 and 23.758/2026, it involves the random selection of polling sections by auditors, political parties, and oversight entities to validate vote-count accuracy and detect any interference.

item.title: TSE realiza Corrida Pela Democracia neste domingo (9)
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) will hold the Race for Democracy this Sunday (9), closing the National Week of the Electronic Voting System. The event, featuring TSE President Minister Kassio Nunes Marques, includes three categories: a 2.5 km walk, a 5.3 km race (one lap), and a 10.6 km race (two laps) at the Nelson Piquet International Autodrome in Brasília. Participant kits can be picked up until Friday (7) from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. at the TSE headquarters, while press credentials must be requested by 12 p.m. on Friday and collected from 2 p.m. to 5 p.m. the same day.

item.title: Viralizou: sistema eletrônico de votação não permite alteração do voto
item.description: Brazil's electronic voting system is safeguarded by multiple layers of security, including digital signatures, sealing, source code inspection, and public tests, which prevent any alteration of votes recorded in the voting machines. These measures ensure that only official programs from the Electoral Justice are executed and that any tampering attempt is detected and blocked.

item.title: Diplomata dos EUA participará de reunião no TSE após Brasil negar visto a oficiais americanos
item.description: The TSE will host around 40 diplomats, including a U.S. Embassy representative, to present Brazil's electronic voting system and counter disinformation. The meeting takes place a month after Brazil denied visas to two U.S. officials seeking to challenge the electoral system, amid false claims by Flávio Bolsonaro about Venezuelan origins of the voting machines, which the TSE has publicly refuted.
